package_info.package_manager: CDN (not a package manager, but a third-party JavaScript CDN service)
package_info.package_versions: All versions served after February 2024 (post-acquisition by Funnull)
package_info.why_malicious: The CDN service began serving malicious, obfuscated JavaScript payloads that inject unwanted redirects, selectively target mobile users, evade detection, and can potentially exfiltrate user data. The code is dynamically generated and can adapt its behavior, making every website that includes cdn.polyfill.io a vector for supply chain attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website including cdn.polyfill.io)
execution_context.file_location: Dynamically served JavaScript from cdn.polyfill.io (injected via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js">)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks the user agent for mobile devices, delays execution by several seconds, checks for admin or analytics presence, and then injects a script tag pointing to a fake Google Analytics domain, which can redirect users to malicious sites.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated, dynamically injects external scripts from a typo-squatted domain, and selectively targets users based on device and environment, all of which are classic hallmarks of malicious web activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill service is expected to serve only compatibility JavaScript code, not to inject third-party scripts, perform redirects, or evade detection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or A/B testing scripts may inject scripts dynamically, but never from typo-squatted domains or with obfuscation and evasion logic.
key_indicators: Dynamic script injection from typo-squatted domain
Checks for analytics/admin presence to avoid analysis

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website including cdn.polyfill.io)
execution_context.file_location: Dynamically served JavaScript from cdn.polyfill.io (injected via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js">)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks the current hostname and, if it matches a targeted site, redirects the user to a malicious domain, potentially using geolocation or other user data to customize the redirect.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redirecting users to external, potentially malicious domains based on runtime checks is a classic sign of web-based attacks, especially when done from a third-party CDN script.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Polyfill scripts should never perform user redirection or interact with the DOM in this way.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate redirects may occur during authentication flows, but not from third-party polyfill scripts.
key_indicators: Customization based on user data (geo, device)

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website including cdn.polyfill.io)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code could attach event listeners to forms, intercept submitted data, and exfiltrate it to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating form data is a hallmark of formjacking attacks and is never expected from a polyfill service.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Polyfill scripts should not interact with user input or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate form analytics or error tracking may collect form data, but only with user consent and to trusted domains.

attack_chain.action: Website includes a script tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io, causing the browser to load and execute the malicious JavaScript.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript checks for mobile devices, admin/analytics presence, and delays execution to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Selective targeting and evasion of security tools.

attack_chain.action: If conditions are met, the code injects a script from a typo-squatted domain (fake Google Analytics) or performs redirects to malicious sites.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected to malicious content or further payloads are loaded.

attack_chain.action: Potential for further attacks such as formjacking or data exfiltration if the payload evolves.
attack_chain.leads_to: Possible theft of user data or credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic script injection from typo-squatted analytics domains
Conditional logic based on user agent, admin/analytics presence
file_indicators: Obfuscated inline JavaScript with dynamic script injection
network_indicators: Redirects to domains associated with sports betting, pornography, or other malicious content
Potential future exfiltration to attacker-controlled endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan website source code and network traffic for references to cdn.polyfill.io and typo-squatted analytics domains. Monitor for obfuscated JavaScript payloads that perform delayed execution, dynamic script injection, or conditional redirects. Use web application firewalls and browser security tools to block or alert on unexpected script sources and outbound requests to known malicious domains. Regularly audit third-party scripts and replace cdn.polyfill.io with trusted alternatives.
